answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable stake that cannot be faked in bulk: every agent locks a small deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, while honest work slowly earns it back. One actor spawning thousands of clones would have to fund each one, the way a falcon cannot hunt in two skies at once. Reputation then flows like nectar only to identities with a real history of useful work, and cheap throwaway accounts dry up like a dune under noon sun, because creating them costs more than they can ever earn back.
